reason: The proposed scratch lifetime change is small and keeps the existing layout and compute path; its performance benefit is unknown. The B-panel layout directly tests the requested packing tradeoff and is expressible, but adds timed packing and changes traversal. A 32-bit K counter is a narrow, low-risk change with uncertain code-generation impact. Reordering ZA operations is also expressible, but may change rounding. The two N=64 proposals describe the same experiment and need a helper that is not supplied, so they rank together and cannot proceed without host preparation. Transpose fusion has the largest register-level and correctness risk, and repeats A loads across output panels. Historical packed-B results regressed, while panel32 variants did not show repeatable gains; neither result establishes how these distinct proposals will perform.
